name: CAVA Group, Inc.

profile.description: CAVA Group owns and operates fast-casual Mediterranean restaurants under the CAVA brand in the United States and sells dips and spreads through grocery retail. Founded in 2006 and headquartered in Washington, D.C., CAVA IPO'd in June 2023 and converted the Zoe's Kitchen chain acquired in 2018. Q2 2026 revenue rose 31.3% to $365.4M, with same-restaurant sales up 9.0% and traffic up 5.3%. FY2026 guidance (reaffirmed) calls for 4.5-6.5% same-restaurant sales growth and 75-77 net new restaurants, with adjusted EBITDA guidance raised in May to $181-191M. TTM revenue is $1.37B. FY2025 revenue was $1.18B, up from $500M in FY2021.

innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): CAVA converted the Zoe's Kitchen chain acquired in 2018 into CAVA units and built a grocery dips-and-spreads business, growing revenue from $500M (FY2021) to $1.18B (FY2025) [5][2]. That is one significant transformation that opened a national growth runway. AI Deployment (1/2): The Connected Kitchen generative-AI system, which monitors ingredient usage and alerts staff on prep and batch amounts, is live in four restaurants after a pilot, and a kitchen display system is in test at 25 locations [2]. There are no quantified savings yet. Market Share (2/2): CAVA is the category-defining Mediterranean fast-casual chain, growing revenue 31.3% with 9.0% same-restaurant sales and 5.3% traffic growth in Q2 2026, following 9.7% same-restaurant sales in Q1 [1]. Pipeline (2/2): 75-77 net new restaurant openings are guided for FY2026, giving specific unit-growth visibility [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): The company discloses no R&D spending (typical of restaurants) [5].
innovation.label: STRONG

inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): CAVA's mission to 'bring heart, health and humanity to food' is distinctive. Leadership treats it as a strategic tool: Schulman measures culture like any other operating metric and built a mission, values and competencies framework [2][3]. The mission has not been validated over decades. Community Impact (1/2): CAVA published its first Impact Report in July 2025 and a 2025 Impact Update in June 2026 under the 'Heart, Health and Humanity' banner [3]. This is general corporate impact reporting without dollar-quantified signature programs. Employee Retention (0/2): The company is investing in an assistant general manager program to strengthen the leadership pipeline, but no retention or tenure data was found [2]. Insider Buying (0/2): Insiders have been heavy net sellers. A July 2026 Delaware derivative suit alleges founders, directors and backers sold ~$2.2B of stock, including nearly $500M by board and management between August 2024 and March 2025 [4].
inspiration.label: DEVELOPING

infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock (no dividend). D/E 61.9% (score 1.0, 1x); ROE 8.3% (0.555, 2x); revenue growth 31.3% YoY (1.0, 1x); revenue CAGR 23.9% (FY2021-FY2025, 4 years, the longest FMP history available; 1.0, 2x); Forward P/E 79.1 (0.0, 1x); profit margin 4.8% (0.241, 1x); Forward PEG 5.11 per Yahoo (0.0, 2x) [1][5]. Weighted sum 5.35 / 10 = 5.35, rounded to 5. The fundamentals are strong but the valuation is very rich. Liquidity is well clear of the floor: 3.32M average volume x $58.74 = ~$195M a day.
infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING

ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): A restaurant serving freshly prepared food in physical locations cannot be substituted by AI, and no analyst flags AI as a disruption risk to CAVA's demand [1][2]. Schulman frames AI as a tool to 'enhance the human experience' of guests rather than replace hospitality, and is using it for kitchen productivity through Connected Kitchen [2]. AI Opportunity (0/1): CAVA generates no AI revenue; its AI use is internal efficiency only.
ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens, CAVA has a real cause in heart, health and humanity, and a CEO who treats culture as the operating system. The decision to convert Zoe's Kitchen rather than run it for cash showed a willingness to invest for the long term. The heavy insider selling and the derivative suit over it, together with a growth story priced at 79x forward earnings, pull the company toward finite-game pressures.

just_cause.analysis: 2/3 pts. 'Heart, health and humanity' is a genuine cause that links food to wellbeing and community, and leadership has built a formal values framework around it [2][3]. It is partially lived and has not been tested by a downturn as a public company.

trusting_teams.analysis: 1/2 pts. Schulman says culture 'is the catalyst for everything' and has invested in GM and assistant-GM development [2]. No independent employee-sentiment or retention data was found to confirm a high-trust environment, and restaurant labor is inherently high-turnover.

worthy_rivals.analysis: 0/1 pts. No management commentary was found that frames rivals such as Chipotle or Sweetgreen as worthy rivals. Public messaging centers on CAVA's own traffic and share gains [1][2].

existential_flexibility.analysis: 1/2 pts. Buying Zoe's Kitchen in 2018 and converting it to CAVA was a significant strategic move, and Schulman refocused the company on five core priorities to stabilize it afterward [2]. The core concept was expanded, not reinvented.

courage_to_lead.analysis: 1/2 pts. The capital-intensive Zoe's conversions and continued investment in an extra management layer during a period of consumer strain show a willingness to sacrifice near-term margin [2]. However, large insider sales near the stock's peak undercut the signal of long-term conviction [4].

investment_thesis: CAVA is one of the few restaurant chains growing traffic and units at the same time. Q2 2026 revenue rose 31.3% to $365.4M, with same-restaurant sales up 9.0% on 5.3% traffic growth [1]. Management reaffirmed 75-77 net new restaurants and 4.5-6.5% same-restaurant sales growth for FY2026 and raised adjusted EBITDA guidance to $181-191M [1]. Revenue has compounded at ~24% a year since 2021, D/E is a modest 61.9%, and Connected Kitchen AI tools are rolling out to raise unit productivity [2][5].
thesis_continued: The bear case is valuation and governance. At 79x forward earnings with a Yahoo PEG of 5.1, the stock prices in years of flawless execution, and reaffirmed same-store guidance implies a second-half slowdown from the 9-10% pace of the first half [1]. Insiders and founding backers sold an alleged ~$2.2B of stock, now the subject of a July 2026 Delaware derivative suit, and a 2022 PFAS packaging class action remains a reputational overhang [4]. Profit margin is just 4.8%, ROE is 8.3%, and free cash flow is roughly breakeven per Yahoo Finance as the company funds rapid unit growth [5].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results: whether same-restaurant sales hold near the 9% Q2 pace or decelerate toward the 4.5-6.5% full-year guidance [1]
Delivery of 75-77 net new restaurants in FY2026 and new-market openings extending national scale [1]
Wider rollout of Connected Kitchen generative-AI and kitchen display systems (currently live in 4 and in test at 25 restaurants) lifting restaurant-level margins [2]
key_risks: Valuation compression: Forward P/E of 79x and PEG of 5.1 leave little room for any same-store slowdown [5]
Governance overhang from the July 2026 Delaware derivative suit alleging ~$2.2B of insider sales at inflated prices [4]
Consumer-spending pressure on fast casual, plus the pending PFAS packaging class action affecting brand perception [4]
